headings.title: Introduction to Critical Care Diagnostics
headings.content: Diagnostic investigations in the intensive care unit guide immediate, life-saving interventions. Unlike routine hospital wards where tests follow a steady schedule, critical care diagnostics occur continuously and simultaneously. Nurses must rapidly interpret data while managing multiple complex therapies. The main goal is identifying rapid physiological changes before irreversible organ failure sets in.

headings.title: Hemodynamic Monitoring and Arterial Lines
headings.content:
Hemodynamic monitoring evaluates blood flow and pressure within the cardiovascular system. An arterial line provides continuous, beat-to-beat blood pressure measurement and easy access for frequent blood sampling.

- **Zeroing**: Calibrating the transducer to atmospheric pressure at the phlebostatic axis.
- **Dampening**: Assessing waveform quality to ensure accurate readings.
- **Allen Test**: Evaluating collateral ulnar circulation before radial cannulation.

headings.title: Arterial Blood Gas Analysis
headings.content:
Arterial blood gas analysis measures acid-base balance, ventilation, and oxygenation status. Drawing samples requires strict adherence to aseptic technique, usually from an indwelling arterial line or via direct radial puncture. 

| Parameter | Normal Range |
| --- | --- |
| pH | 7.35 - 7.45 |
| PaCO2 | 35 - 45 mmHg |
| PaO2 | 80 - 100 mmHg |
| HCO3 | 22 - 26 mEq/L |

headings.title: Laboratory Biomarkers and Hematology
headings.content: Laboratory panels in critical care track multi-organ function, infection, and tissue injury. Cardiac troponins detect myocardial ischemia, while serum lactate signals cellular hypoxia and shock. Complete blood counts and coagulation profiles alert the nurse to bleeding risks or disseminated intravascular coagulation. Serial testing matters more than single values because trends reveal whether therapies are working.

headings.title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound
headings.content: Point-of-care ultrasound allows clinicians to visualize anatomical structures and pathologies directly at the bedside. Critical care nurses and doctors use it to assess volume status, guide central venous catheter insertions, and detect pneumothoraces rapidly. This imaging modality reduces transport risks for unstable patients because the machine comes directly to the bedside.

headings.title: Advanced Imaging and Neurological Monitoring
headings.content: Advanced imaging like computed tomography scans provide detailed cross-sectional views of the brain, chest, and abdomen. Electroencephalography and intracranial pressure monitors track neurological status in patients with traumatic brain injury or stroke. Transporting these vulnerable patients requires coordinated teamwork, portable monitors, and continuous respiratory support.

headings.title: Nursing Responsibilities and Patient Safety
headings.content: Nurses play a central role in preparing patients, maintaining equipment, and interpreting basic diagnostic trends. Patient safety depends on verifying identity, ensuring equipment is calibrated, and responding promptly to abnormal alarms. Nurses also provide comfort and explanation to conscious patients undergoing frightening bedside procedures.
